notes: Covers the NV360 Series, a bagless upright with a detachable Lift-Away pod. The 120 V ~ 60 Hz, 1200 W rating on the owner's guide's specification page is for the whole vacuum, not for the motor.

gaps: Filter numbers conflict: the owner's guide gives XFF350 (pre-motor) and XHF350 (post-motor HEPA); the researcher reported Shark's product page listing XFF500 and XHF500 under the Lift-Away family. That page was not re-opened; only the guide's numbers are recorded.
No part numbers for the brushroll motor, belt or motherboard appear in the iFixit guides.
The guide does not say which motor the thermostat switches off or where the main motor sits, so the motor entry gives no location and no rating.
The brushroll motor is filed under motor_universal as a catalogue bucket only; no source gives its type or rating.
The belt steps shown in iFixit guide 98642 come from the NV500 belt guide 98443, which iFixit lists as its prerequisite; the guide's own introduction says the belt must come off before the motor.
iFixit comments report Torx screws and more screws than the guide's six 15 mm Phillips; only the guide's version is recorded.
Left out: cord length, hose length, and any switch, motor or board ratings.
method: Shark NV360 Series Owner's Guide (PDF on pdf.lowes.com, file NV360_series_IB_E_Mv14, 2020), read with tools/research.js pdf: cords and polarized plug on PDF p. 2, brushroll indicator on p. 3, On/Off switch on p. 4, filter kits on pp. 6-7, thermostat and stretch hose on p. 8, specifications on p. 9.
iFixit guides 98642 (roller brush motor) and 98643 (motherboard) read through the iFixit API and as web pages; both are filed under Shark Navigator Lift-Away Deluxe NV360.
iFixit content is CC BY-NC-SA; only facts and links are used.
No bot check or login wall on any page read.

comps.spec: Vacuum motor: the guide says a thermostat switches the motor off when the vacuum overheats (whole-unit rating is in the notes)
Roller brush motor that lifts out of a half-cylindrical holder in the motorized floor brush compartment; two wires end in metal connectors under blue plastic insulation
Black roller brush belt: pulled over the end of the roller brush and slid off the end of the motor by hand; it has to come off before the brush motor can be replaced
Motherboard held by two 10 mm screws in the motorized floor brush compartment; the two wires that ran to the roller brush motor are cut off it and soldered back on reassembly
Three-position On/Off switch: O off, I suction only (bare floors), II brushroll on (carpets and area rugs) (PDF p. 4)
Power cord with a polarized plug, stored around two cord hooks (PDF pp. 2, 6)
Pre-motor filter kit XFF350: a foam filter and a felt filter, both pulled out of the top of the pod; rinsed with water, air-dried at least 24 hours, cleaned every 3 months (PDF pp. 6-7)
Post-motor HEPA filter XHF350, pulled out from behind a cover at the front of the vacuum; rinsed with water, air-dried 24 hours, cleaned every 2 years (PDF pp. 6-7)
Thermostat that turns the motor off when the vacuum overheats; restart steps are to empty the dust cup, clean the filters, clear blockages and let it cool at least 60 minutes (PDF p. 8)
Stretch hose on the back of the portable Lift-Away pod, released by squeezing its tabs and pulling up (PDF p. 8)
